pages.note: The chant continuing; no heading. Twenty-six TWO-COLUMN rows (gutter measured at 248px, x 759-1006). Four more groups of the roll-call — the Samānas and the devas corrupted by play, the Sukkas and Pajunna the rain-god, the Khemiyas up to the Paranimmita devas — then the count of sixty orders and the verse in which they all come to see the Nāga.

checks.issue: A THIRD GUTTER MEASURE IN THREE CONSECUTIVE SHEETS — 179 was 251px at x 801-1051, 180 was 165px at x 943-1107, and this sheet is 248px at x 759-1006. Same chant, same printer, three settings. Each was ink-profiled and none was carried over from the sheet before. The row count was confirmed twice over: profiling the LEFT column alone and the RIGHT column alone each returns exactly 26 bands.

⚠ THE SHEET PUNCTUATES ITS OWN REPEATED LINES INCONSISTENTLY, and this was checked exhaustively rather than sampled: the end of ALL 26 right-column lines was cropped at 8× and read one by one. Every mark on the sheet is a round FULL STOP; there is not a single comma anywhere on it. But the two refrain lines do not take the same mark each time they appear. `สัพเพ นานัตตะวัณณิโน` closes the count at verses 127, 134, 140 and 143 and carries NO mark at 127, 134 and 143 but a FULL STOP at 140. `วัณณะวันโต ยะสัสสิโน` closes the middle line at verses 121, 128, 135 and 141 and carries NO mark at 121 and 141 but a FULL STOP at 128 and 135. The roman twin is consistent at every one of these — comma after the count, full stop after the middle line. Entered as each line prints it; nothing levelled.

⚠ นิมมานะระติโน IS PRINTED WITH PLAIN น, giving `nimmānaratino`, where the roman twin verse 164 sets `Nimmāṇaratino` with the retroflex ṇ. These are the devas who delight in creating, and the canon has ṇ. Read at 2.4×; the glyph is น and sits on the baseline without ณ's foot. Entered as this page prints it.

A WORD-DIVISION DIFFERENCE FROM THE TWIN, letters identical. This sheet sets จันทังวะ as one word, giving `candaṃva`; the roman copy's verse 171 sets `candaṃ va` as two. Entered as this page prints it.

A PUNCTUATION DIFFERENCE FROM THE TWIN. The roman copy breaks this line with a full stop in the middle — `Khiḍḍāpadūsikā āgū. Āgū manopadūsikā.` — where this sheet runs it straight through with no mark until the end. The twin does the same thing again at verse 139, `Nimmāṇaratino āgū. Athāgū paranimmitā.`, and again this sheet has no mid-line mark. Entered as this page prints it, both times.

A PUNCTUATION DIFFERENCE FROM THE TWIN. The roman copy's verse 158 sets a comma after pajunno — `Thanayaṃ āgā pajunno, yo disā abhivassati.` — where this sheet has no mark there. Entered as this page prints it.

THE CLOSING SPEECH IS UNMARKED ON THIS SHEET. The roman twin ends its verse 169 with a COLON and wraps verses 170-171 in quotation marks, making the last two lines the devas' own words. This page prints all three plain, with no colon and no quotes. Entered as printed; the English keeps the sense of reported speech even though the Pali carries no marks.

ปะทูสิกา IS SET WITH A LONG ู at both verses 124 and 139-adjacent occurrences, giving `padūsikā`, where most editions have `padosikā`. ⚠ THE TWIN AGREES — its verse 149 also reads `Khiḍḍāpadūsikā` and `manopadūsikā`. Both copies of this book say ū, so this is the book's own reading throughout and not a fault in one copy.
THE CLUSTER MARK IS THANTHAKHAT ์ AGAIN — นามัน์วะเยนะ at verse 144, the only one on this sheet. That matches the rest of the chant, which sets ์ and never yamakkan ๎.

THE COUNT CHANGES AT THIS VERSE. Every earlier group closed with `ทะเสเต ทะสะธา กายา`, ten hosts; here it becomes `สัฏเฐเต เทวะนิกายา`, sixty orders of devas — the sum of all the groups counted so far. Read carefully because the line looks like the refrain at a glance and is not. The twin's verse 168 agrees.
THE SHEET OPENS MID-REFRAIN. Verses 121 and 122 complete the group whose count line closed page 180 on a comma; the page turn falls inside the three-line refrain, as it did between 178 and 179.

verses.pali: อิทธิมันโต ชุติมันโต วัณณะวันโต ยะสัสสิโน
verses.english: possessed of power, of radiance, of beauty and of renown,

verses.pali: โมทะมานา อะภิกกามุง ภิกขูนัง สะมิติง วะนัง.
verses.english: came rejoicing to the wood, to the assembly of bhikkhus.

verses.pali: สะมานา มะหาสะมานา มานุสา มานุสุตตะมา
verses.english: The Samāna devas and the Mahāsamānas, the Mānusas and Mānusuttamas,

verses.english: the Pāragas and the Mahāpāragas came, devas of renown.

verses.pali: ทะเสเต ทะสะธา กายา สัพเพ นานัตตะวัณณิโน

verses.pali_roman: Thanayaṃ āgā pajunno yo disā abhivassati.
verses.english: and thundering came Pajunna, who rains upon the quarters.

verses.pali_roman: Khemiyā tusitā yāmā kaṭṭhakā ca yasassino
verses.english: The Khemiyas, the Tusitas and the Yāmas, and the Kaṭṭhakas of renown,

verses.pali: ลัมพิตะกา ลามะเสฏฐา โชตินามา จะ อาสะวา.
verses.english: the Lambitakas and the Lāmaseṭṭhas, the Jotināmas and the Āsavas.

verses.pali: นิมมานะระติโน อาคู อะถาคู ปะระนิมมิตา
verses.english: The devas delighting in creation came, and then those who wield what others create.
